duration.text: The Quantitative Economics at Xiamen University is a 2 Years long program for international students, taught in English.

fees.text: Application Fee: $ 150 USD Service Fee: $ 50 USD Tuition fee: $ 6250 USD/per year ￥ 45000 CNY/per year

materials.text: 1.Photocopy of valid passport With photo, passport number &expiration date and name included. 2.Passport-sized photo A passport-sized photo taken recently of the applicant. 3.Master's degree diploma Graduation certificate should be in Chinese or English. If not, it should be translated into Chinese or English and be notarized. 4.Transcript of postgraduate school 5.Health certificate Required during application.Photocopy of notarized foreigner physical examination record (for durations of study over 6 months) 6.English proficiency test certificate For example, IELTS or TOEFL, only for applicant whose native language is not English. 7.Two letters of recommendation From professor or associate professor or equivalents 8.Study plan Explaining your studies, work experiences and research plan. You should also give information of any academic publications or other scholarly achievements you believe may be relevant.(no less than 1000 words, in English or Chinese) 9.Financial support statement Photocopy of the financial support statement with signature

requirements.text: 1.Hold a non-Chinese passport and pass the required health check for visa holders in China . 2.Hold a recognized bachelor degree or above, or equivalent. 3.Have obtained a minimum score of 550 points or above for Old TOEFL, 80 points or above for New TOEFL, grade 6.0 or above for IELTS, or on presentation of a certificate from some other approved test of English proficiency. Native English speakers and applicants whose teaching language during undergraduate studies is English are exempt from this requirement. Other candidates whose university courses were taught in English will be considered on a case by case basis. 4.The ability to demonstrate relevant professional experience will be given individual consideration.
